messages.content:
Criteria:
- P1: Dependencies: does every step come after the steps whose results it needs? If a requirement of step B uses something that a requirement of step A creates (a name, a command, a connection, data, a schema, a part that is reused), B needs A. Name each missing dependency as 'A -> B' (A must finish before B) and say what B needs from A.
- P2: Coverage: is each requirement's work done by build and test steps that really do it?
- P3: Acceptance criteria: are they concrete and checkable?
- P4: Granularity: no duplicated steps and no step split into trivial pieces?

The research, verify, design and review steps and the order research -> design -> build -> test -> documents -> review come from a template and are correct. Steps listed as 'after: X' already depend on X (directly); a dependency through other steps also counts.

Material:
Requirements:
R1 [must] Write a 2000-word report comparing two version control systems.
R2 [must] The report must discuss the branching and merging models of both systems.
R3 [must] Include at least five academic references.
R4 [must] Summarise the findings in a conclusion section.
R5 [could] You may include diagrams of each workflow.

Plan steps:
research [research] Research the topic (requirements: -; after: -) criteria: every research question has an answer with sources
verify [research] Check the research findings (requirements: -; after: research) criteria: every claim the document uses is supported by a source
design [design] Outline the document (requirements: -; after: verify) criteria: every requirement has a section in the outline
T1 [implement] Draft report introduction and overview (requirements: R1; after: design) criteria: Report includes a clear introduction of both version control systems; Word count for this section contributes to total ≤ 2000 words
T2 [implement] Describe branching and merging models (requirements: R2; after: T1) criteria: Branching and merging models of both systems are explained; Comparison highlights similarities and differences
T3 [implement] Add academic references in APA style (requirements: R3; after: T2) criteria: At least five academic references are listed; All citations and bibliography follow APA style
T5 [implement] Create optional workflow diagrams (requirements: R5; after: T2) criteria: Diagrams for both systems are included; Diagrams are clear and labeled
T4 [implement] Write conclusion summarising findings (requirements: R4; after: T3) criteria: Conclusion section restates key findings; Conclusion ties back to introduction and analysis
T6 [test] Check word count and APA compliance (requirements: R1, R3; after: T5, T4) criteria: Total word count ≤ 2000; APA citation style is correct throughout
T7 [test] Validate branching and merging discussion (requirements: R2; after: T4, T5) criteria: Branching and merging models are accurately described; Comparison addresses both systems equally
T8 [test] Confirm presence of conclusion (requirements: R4; after: T4, T5) criteria: Conclusion section is present; It summarises the main findings
T9 [test] Review optional diagrams (requirements: R5; after: T5, T4) criteria: Diagrams are present for both systems; They are correctly referenced in the text
T10 [document] Prepare Report (requirements: -; after: T6, T7, T8, T9) criteria: D1 exists: Report as PDF; it matches the finished, tested work
review [review] Final review (requirements: -; after: T10) criteria: every must requirement is met; every deliverable is present; C1 respected: Use APA citation style.; C2 respected: The report may not exceed 2000 words.
